result.output:
1	import ProjectDescription
2	
3	/// The app and its widget extension are separate processes with separate
4	/// containers, so anything both must read — the known robots, the snapshot the
5	/// widget renders — lives in this group rather than in either container.
6	let appGroup = "group.com.alexey1312.ReachyMini"
7	
8	let project = Project(
9	    name: "ReachyMiniApps",
10	    packages: [
11	        // Local ReachyKit SPM package at the repo root
12	        .package(path: ".."),
13	        // Prefire renders SwiftUI previews as snapshots and as a browsable playbook. It is
14	        // declared here rather than in Package.swift because its generated tests and its
15	        // PlaybookView both call UIKit unconditionally — the root package still builds for macOS.
16	        // Exact, not `upToNextMajor`: `ReachyUISnapshotTests/PreviewTests.stencil` is a fork of
17	        // this version's built-in test template, and a floated minor would render it against a
18	        // changed set of Stencil arguments.
19	        .remote(url: "https://github.com/BarredEwe/Prefire", requirement: .exact("5.7.0")),
20	        .remote(
21	            url: "https://github.com/pointfreeco/swift-snapshot-testing",
22	            requirement: .upToNextMajor(from: "1.19.4")
23	        ),
24	    ],
25	    settings: .settings(
26	        // One version for the app and the widget: App Store validation requires
27	        // the extension's CFBundleShortVersionString to match its host's.
28	        base: [
29	            // Beta: the first tag is 0.1.0, and the tag and the shipped version
30	            // have to be the same number to be worth reading.
31	            "MARKETING_VERSION": "0.2.3",
32	            "CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION": "1",
33	        ],
34	        configurations: [
35	            // Set project-wide rather than per target: the previews and the playbook reach ReachyUI's
36	            // internal screens through `@testable import`, and it is the *package* target that has to
37	            // be built with testability for that to link.
38	            .debug(name: .debug, settings: ["ENABLE_TESTABILITY": "YES"]),
39	            .release(name: .release),
40	        ]
41	    ),
42	    targets: [
43	        .target(
44	            name: "ReachyMini",
45	            destinations: [.iPhone, .iPad, .mac],
46	            product: .app,
47	            bundleId: "com.alexey1312.ReachyMini",
48	            deploymentTargets: .multiplatform(iOS: "18.0", macOS: "15.0"),
49	            infoPlist: .extendingDefault(with: [
50	                // The product name is the internal identifier; this is the brand.
51	                "CFBundleDisplayName": .string("Hey Reachy"),
52	                "CFBundleName": .string("Hey Reachy"),
53	                // What `\(.applicationName)` in `ReachyShortcuts` resolves to, and
54	                // the display name alone reads badly inside a phrase: "Wake up Hey
55	                // Reachy". Siri matches every phrase against these as well.
56	                // Deliberately not "Reachy Mini" — that is the name of Pollen's own
57	                // app, and on a phone carrying both it would be ambiguous.
58	                // **Siri only, and it is not a Spotlight key** — QA1950 describes it
59	                // as the spoken form and says nothing about typed search, so adding
60	                // a word here does nothing for a query in the search field. That
61	                // half is `Navigation/SpotlightIndex.swift`. Apple's own note there:
62	                // put synonyms in it, never the display name itself.
63	                "INAlternativeAppNames": .array([
64	                    .dictionary(["INAlternativeAppName": .string("Reachy")]),
65	                ]),
66	                "CFBundleShortVersionString": .string("$(MARKETING_VERSION)"),
67	                "CFBundleVersion": .string("$(CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION)"),
68	                // Spelled out because `actool` does not write it: it fills
69	                // CFBundleIcons from the catalogue and leaves the top level
70	                // empty, which App Store Connect rejects the upload over. Found
71	                // by unpacking the exported .ipa, not by any build warning.
72	                "CFBundleIconName": .string("AppIcon"),
73	                // ITMS-90683: WebRTC (and RealityKit via ARKit) reference the
74	                // capture APIs, so the string is required even though the app
75	                // never records with the phone's camera. Say exactly that.
76	                "NSCameraUsageDescription": .string(
77	                    "Hey Reachy never records with your phone's camera; the robot video stack references this API."
78	                ),
79	                // HTTPS-exempt encryption only; answered here once so App Store
80	                // Connect never asks per build.
81	                "ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption": .boolean(false),
82	                "LSApplicationCategoryType": .string("public.app-category.utilities"),
83	                // Phase 0.4 device checks: Local Network permission + Bonjour + ATS
84	                "NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription": .string(
85	                    "Discovers and connects to your Reachy Mini robot on the local network."
86	                ),
87	                "NSBonjourServices": .array([
88	                    .string("_reachy-mini._tcp"),
89	                    .string("_http._tcp"),
90	                ]),
91	                "NSAppTransportSecurity": .dictionary([
92	                    "NSAllowsLocalNetworking": .boolean(true),
93	                ]),
94	                // BLE Wi-Fi provisioning. The only key a foreground central needs on
95	                // iOS 18: no capability, and no pairing prompt either, since the robot
96	                // registers a NoInputNoOutput Just-Works agent.
97	                // NSBluetoothPeripheralUsageDescription is iOS 12 and earlier — omitted.
98	                "NSBluetoothAlwaysUsageDescription": .string(
99	                    "Sets up your Reachy Mini's Wi-Fi and recovers a robot that can't reach the network."
100	                ),
101	                // Phase 2 camera: WebRTC mic uplink (client mic → robot speaker)
102	                "NSMicrophoneUsageDescription": .string(
103	                    "Talk to people near your Reachy Mini through its speaker."
104	                ),
105	                "UILaunchScreen": .dictionary([:]),
106	                // Read by `KnownRobots`, which is in a library and so cannot know
107	                // one developer account's group. The extension declares the same.
108	                "ReachyAppGroupIdentifier": .string(appGroup),
109	                // The widget opens the app through this scheme. It is the one the
110	                // OAuth callback already uses: an app gets a scheme, and
111	                // `ASWebAuthenticationSession` claims the callback while a sign-in
112	                // is running regardless of what is registered here.
113	                "CFBundleURLTypes": .array([
114	                    .dictionary([
115	                        "CFBundleURLName": .string("com.alexey1312.ReachyMini"),
116	                        "CFBundleURLSchemes": .array([.string("reachy-mini-swift")]),
117	                    ]),
118	                ]),
119	                // The literal value of `CSSearchableItemActionType`, which is how a
120	                // tapped Spotlight row reaches `RootLifecycle`. Sources disagree
121	                // about whether a *system* activity type has to be declared here at
122	                // all — a custom one certainly does — and the failure mode if it
123	                // does is silent: the rows are found, the tap opens the app, and it
124	                // lands on whatever tab was last selected. Declaring it costs one
125	                // line and settles the question. `Navigation/SpotlightIndex.swift`.
126	                "NSUserActivityTypes": .array([
127	                    .string("com.apple.corespotlightitem"),
128	                ]),
129	            ]),
130	            sources: ["ReachyMini/Sources/**"],
131	            // The five themed icons are iOS-only inputs. macOS has no alternate
132	            // icons at all, so its `actool` compiles them and then drops them —
133	            // measured: the macOS `Assets.car` carries `AppIcon` and nothing else.
134	            // Scoping them saves that work. It is **not** what fixed the macOS asset
135	            // compilation on CI — that needed a newer Xcode, and `ci.yml` says which.
136	            resources: [
137	                .glob(
138	                    pattern: "ReachyMini/Resources/**",
139	                    excluding: ["ReachyMini/Resources/AppIcon-*.icon"]
140	                ),
141	                .glob(
142	                    pattern: "ReachyMini/Resources/AppIcon-*.icon",
143	                    inclusionCondition: .when([.ios])
144	                ),
145	            ],
146	            dependencies: [
147	                .package(product: "ReachyKit"),
148	                .package(product: "ReachyUI"),
149	                // The intents live there so the widget extension can reach the same
150	                // ones; the shortcuts provider that exposes them to Siri has to be
151	                // in this bundle.
152	                .package(product: "ReachyWidgetUI"),
153	                // iOS only, and conditional so the macOS build of this app does not
154	                // try to embed an extension that has no macOS destination.
155	                .target(name: "ReachyWidget", condition: .when([.ios])),
156	            ],
157	            // Two files rather than one generated dictionary: the macOS build is
158	            // sandboxed and hardened for Developer ID, and those keys are
159	            // macOS-only — signing an iOS build with them fails against any
160	            // provisioning profile. The `[sdk=macosx*]` override picks per SDK.
161	            settings: .settings(base: [
162	                "SWIFT_VERSION": "6.0",
163	                "CODE_SIGN_ENTITLEMENTS": "ReachyMini/Entitlements/ReachyMini-iOS.entitlements",
164	                "CODE_SIGN_ENTITLEMENTS[sdk=macosx*]": "ReachyMini/Entitlements/ReachyMini-macOS.entitlements",
165	                // Notarization rejects a Developer ID app without it: the executable
166	                // signs with flags=0x0 and the notary answers "does not have the
167	                // hardened runtime enabled" per architecture.
168	                "ENABLE_HARDENED_RUNTIME[sdk=macosx*]": "YES",
169	                // SDK-scoped because macOS has no alternate icons: an unscoped
170	                // setting names five bundles the macOS build has no use for.
171	                // Every name here must equal a `ReachyTheme.alternateIconName`
172	                // and a committed `.icon` directory — `ThemeIconNameTests` reads
173	                // this literal back and fails when the three drift.
174	                "ASSETCATALOG_COMPILER_ALTERNATE_APPICON_NAMES[sdk=iphone*]":
175	                    "AppIcon-Bronze AppIcon-Teal AppIcon-Indigo AppIcon-Orchid AppIcon-Rose",
176	                "ASSETCATALOG_COMPILER_INCLUDE_ALL_APPICON_ASSETS[sdk=iphone*]": "YES",
177	            ])
178	        ),
179	        // Deliberately thin: a timeline provider over the shared snapshot and a
180	        // view. It depends on ReachyWidgetUI rather than ReachyUI so that a
181	        // process woken for a moment does not link WebRTC and RealityKit.
182	        .target(
183	            name: "ReachyWidget",
184	            destinations: [.iPhone, .iPad],
185	            product: .appExtension,
186	            bundleId: "com.alexey1312.ReachyMini.Widget",
187	            deploymentTargets: .iOS("18.0"),
188	            infoPlist: .extendingDefault(with: [
189	                "CFBundleDisplayName": .string("Hey Reachy"),
190	                "CFBundleShortVersionString": .string("$(MARKETING_VERSION)"),
191	                "CFBundleVersion": .string("$(CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION)"),
192	                "ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption": .boolean(false),
193	                // Its own process, so it needs its own copy of the group name.
194	                "ReachyAppGroupIdentifier": .string(appGroup),
195	                // The control buttons run their intent in *this* process, and it
196	                // talks to the robot over plain HTTP on the LAN. Without the ATS
197	                // exception that request is refused before it leaves the device;
198	                // the usage string is what the system would show if it ever had a
199	                // screen to ask from, which an extension does not — so the
200	                // permission has to already exist from the app having connected.
201	                "NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription": .string(
202	                    "Wakes your Reachy Mini and starts its apps on the local network."
203	                ),
204	                "NSBonjourServices": .array([
205	                    .string("_reachy-mini._tcp"),
206	                    .string("_http._tcp"),
207	                ]),
208	                "NSAppTransportSecurity": .dictionary([
209	                    "NSAllowsLocalNetworking": .boolean(true),
210	                ]),
211	                "NSExtension": .dictionary([
212	                    "NSExtensionPointIdentifier": .string("com.apple.widgetkit-extension"),
213	                ]),
214	            ]),
215	            sources: ["ReachyWidget/Sources/**"],
216	            entitlements: .dictionary([
217	                "com.apple.security.application-groups": .array([.string(appGroup)]),
218	            ]),
219	            dependencies: [
220	                .package(product: "ReachyKit"),
221	                .package(product: "ReachyWidgetUI"),
222	                // Declared even though `ReachyWidgetUI` already links it: Swift needs a
223	                // direct dependency to `import` a module, and this target's controls name
224	                // their titles with `.reachy(_:)`.
225	                .package(product: "ReachyDesign"),
226	            ],
227	            settings: .settings(base: ["SWIFT_VERSION": "6.0"])
228	        ),
229	        // Smoke tests: the one thing snapshots cannot see is the app binary itself
230	        // booting. iOS-only — XCUITest on macOS needs Accessibility permission on
231	        // the runner, which CI cannot grant.
232	        .target(
233	            name: "ReachyMiniUITests",
234	            destinations: [.iPhone, .iPad],
235	            product: .uiTests,
236	            bundleId: "com.alexey1312.ReachyMiniUITests",
237	            deploymentTargets: .iOS("18.0"),
238	            infoPlist: .default,
239	            sources: ["ReachyMiniUITests/Sources/**"],
240	            dependencies: [
241	                .target(name: "ReachyMini"),
242	            ]
243	        ),
244	        .target(
245	            name: "ReachyStorybook",
246	            destinations: [.iPhone, .iPad],
247	            product: .app,
248	            bundleId: "com.alexey1312.ReachyMiniStorybook",
249	            deploymentTargets: .multiplatform(iOS: "18.0"),
250	            infoPlist: .extendingDefault(with: [
251	                // No Bonjour or ATS keys: the storybook renders fixtures and never reaches the network.
252	                "UILaunchScreen": .dictionary([:]),
253	            ]),
254	            // `PrefirePlaybookPlugin` is deliberately absent: it only ever scans the sources of
255	            // the target it is attached to (`GeneratePlaybookCommand` ignores the config's
256	            // `sources`, and `playbook_configuration` has no such key), so it cannot see the
257	            // previews that live in ReachyUI. `mise run storybook` runs the CLI instead.
258	            // `DeviceCheckView` belongs to ReachyMini, which an app target cannot import; its two
259	            // source files are compiled in directly so the catalogue can show that screen too.
260	            sources: [
261	                "ReachyStorybook/Sources/**",
262	                "ReachyStorybook/Generated/**",
263	                "../Sources/ReachyDesign/Previews/**",
264	                "../Sources/ReachyUI/Previews/**",
265	                "../Sources/ReachyWidgetUI/Previews/**",
266	                "ReachyMini/Sources/DeviceCheckView.swift",
267	                "ReachyMini/Sources/DeviceCheckModel.swift",
268	                "ReachyMini/Previews/**",
269	            ],
270	            dependencies: [
271	                .package(product: "ReachyDesign"),
272	                .package(product: "ReachyUI"),
273	                .package(product: "ReachyWidgetUI"),
274	                .package(product: "Prefire"),
275	            ]
276	        ),
277	        .target(
278	            name: "ReachyUISnapshotTests",
279	            destinations: [.iPhone, .iPad],
280	            product: .unitTests,
281	            bundleId: "com.alexey1312.ReachyUISnapshotTests",
282	            deploymentTargets: .multiplatform(iOS: "18.0"),
283	            sources: [
284	                "ReachyUISnapshotTests/Sources/**",
285	                "../Sources/ReachyDesign/Previews/**",
286	                "../Sources/ReachyUI/Previews/**",
287	                "../Sources/ReachyWidgetUI/Previews/**",
288	                "ReachyMini/Sources/DeviceCheckView.swift",
289	                "ReachyMini/Sources/DeviceCheckModel.swift",
290	                "ReachyMini/Previews/**",
291	            ],
292	            dependencies: [
293	                .package(product: "ReachyDesign"),
294	                .package(product: "ReachyUI"),
295	                .package(product: "ReachyWidgetUI"),
296	                .package(product: "Prefire"),
297	                .package(product: "SnapshotTesting"),
298	                .package(product: "PrefireTestsPlugin", type: .plugin),
299	            ]
300	        ),
301	    ]
302	)

content.text: The change is a single string bump: `MARKETING_VERSION` from "0.2.2" to "0.2.3". This is a build/version metadata change with no security-relevant surface — no new entry points, sinks, parsing, permissions, or trust boundaries introduced.
